note: Hand-written inputs for docs/WORKERS.md section 11, written before any implementation of it existed. This is the believing half of the LLM glue: the model call is the application's business (HTTP, retries, a key), and what is comparable across languages is what happens to the answer, which is dirty by nature - fenced, wrapped in prose, with a trailing comma, with tags outside the vocabulary, with a summary longer than the field holds. Section 11 pins the two places where a runtime's default would otherwise decide the contract: whitespace is the ASCII set (Java's trim strips code units below U+0021, Python's strip strips U+00A0), and truncation counts code points (half an emoji is not text). Only the error code is comparable across languages, so the bad-input cases are part of the corpus rather than a comment.

cases.note: the answer arrived exactly as asked for: nothing had to be fixed
a fenced block is stripped, the language tag goes with the fence, and the answer counts as repaired because it did not arrive as the object
the fence is the same fence without a language after it
model output arrives over HTTP with either line ending, so a carriage return is a line ending and not content
the first complete object is the payload and everything else is discarded

input.raw: Here you go: {"tags": ["debut"], "summary": "ok"} Let me know if you need more.

cases.note: the scan counts depth and ignores braces inside JSON strings, so the string closes the object and not the first brace
a backslash escapes exactly the next character, so the escaped quote does not end the string
the one repair the contract specifies, and the answer counts as repaired
the same repair inside an array, with whitespace between the comma and the bracket
a comma inside a string is a character of that string: a repair that removes it there is corrupting data, and this answer is not repaired at all
the object never closes, so there is no payload: no partial recovery, no tags, and the answer is reported as repaired
a model that answered prose is a normal event, not an error: empty tags, empty summary, counts zero, repaired true

input.raw: I am not sure what you want.

cases.note: the empty string is a valid answer and behaves like prose with nothing in it
splitting a free-form string is guessing, not parsing, so a string contributes no tags and no dropped entries
the model writes DEBUT and the application's own label is what comes out

folding is ASCII-only, so IDOL matches idol on every machine. A locale-aware lowercase would map the capital I to a dotless one under a Turkish default locale and silently stop matching - the trap this rule exists to prevent
an unmatched tag is dropped and named, never guessed into a nearby vocabulary entry
duplicates are decided on the matched canonical form: the first occurrence wins and the others are named
the limit applies after deduplication and keeps the model's own order, not the vocabulary's
three different reasons in one answer: an empty tag after trimming, and two elements that are not strings at all
a non-string element is reported as its JSON text with no insignificant whitespace, which is the only way the report is comparable across languages
the summary is measured in code points, so two emoji and two letters with a limit of three keeps two emoji and one letter
the limit falls inside an astral character: a truncation by UTF-16 code units would emit half of one, which is not text and cannot be re-encoded
zero is the absent value here, as in maxTags

whitespace is the ASCII set of section 2 and nothing else: U+00A0 stays part of the tag, so it does not match the vocabulary, and the report names it as it arrived. The tab and the newline around the first tag arrive as JSON escapes, which is the only way they can arrive inside a JSON string

JSON here means RFC 8259: a control character inside a string has to be escaped, so a model that emitted a real newline inside one produced no parseable answer. Nothing is recovered and the answer is reported as repaired. This is pinned because a lenient parser would accept it and quietly return a tag nobody asked for
an astral character in an unmatched tag survives into the report, in byte order with the rest
the report is sorted by value then reason as UTF-8 bytes, so two runs in two languages can be compared as reports and not only as sets
a list where a string was asked for is a prompt problem, not a parse error: the summary is empty and the tags still work

matching folds A-Z and nothing else: the Kelvin sign is not the letter k, and the dotted capital I is not the letter i, so neither matches the vocabulary. A language whose lowercase is Unicode-aware would match both and quietly return tags the application never defined - Python folds the Kelvin sign to k, and a locale-aware lower in Java does worse. Neither is hypothetical: they are one call away in the obvious implementation

JSON here means RFC 8259, so a bare NaN is not a JSON value: there is no payload, nothing is recovered, and the answer counts as repaired. Python's json.loads accepts NaN by default and so do some Java libraries, which turns a malformed answer into a tag nobody asked for
an error answer is comparable through its code
a negative limit is not a limit
a vocabulary the application cannot compare against is a caller bug, not a model bug
